It shows up when an athlete eases up after early success and slowly regresses, when a student settles for “good enough” grades instead of pushing higher, when a leader ignores small warning signs because things seem fine, or when someone relies on past discipline rather than continuing daily growth. Craig Walton Jr. is a name worth knowing—on the field now, and off the field very soon.

Hailing from Camden, New Jersey, Walton is a cornerback for the #LSU Tigers. While his journey at LSU is still unfolding, his discipline and dedication are already evident. During the 2024 season, he appeared in two games on special teams, earning his varsity letter, and was named to the 2024 SEC Academic Honor Roll—an achievement that speaks to his commitment both athletically and academically.

Before Baton Rouge, @cwalt.8 made his mark at Camden High School, where he recorded an impressive 67 tackles during his senior season, including 12 tackles for loss and two sacks. Those numbers tell part of the story—but not all of it.

What stands out just as much as his on-field potential is what he brings off the field. With his height, size, and #athletic build, Walton has all the physical tools to step into the #fashion and #modeling space—an avenue more athletes are smartly exploring as they build long-term brands beyond the game. In today’s era, presence matters, and Craig Walton Jr. has the look, confidence, and background to translate seamlessly into editorial fashion, campaigns, and brand partnerships.

If you want to play third base with confidence, trust your instincts, and become the infielder your team relies on, this is your opportunity to learn directly from someone doing it at the highest level.

athlete.bio: A fierce competitor with a flair for creativity, this guard blends agility and precision on the court. Off the hardwood, a charismatic personality shines, inspiring teammates and fans alike.

caption:
This holiday season, @flaujae has a national championship on her wish list. To Johnson, holiday cheer is about spreading her confidence and joy. She’s even partnered with @dickssportinggoods to help you tackle all your wrapping needs with her custom wrapping paper. How would one wrap up a national championship? For Johnson, making the most of the holidays looks like spending time with her family, working on her music, and “prioritizing me time,” she tells SELF. 

And the LSU senior needs her rest, as she’s just kicked off her final season with the Tigers. The senior guard was last season’s leading scorer, and this year she wants to help guide them to a national championship. But that’s not all she has going for her. “I feel like I’ve just been blessed with two things that I’m good at,” she tells SELF. In addition to being a college basketball star and future WNBA player, she’s also a highly successful rapper.

After graduation, she’s looking forward to what the future holds and hopes it’s being drafted to the WNBA to start her pro career. “Once you go into the WNBA, it’s like you’re a rookie again. You go from being a senior back to a rookie, and you have to prove yourself. And the only way I know how to do that is with the work,” she tells SELF. “So whatever team sees a vision for me, believes in me, and needs me to help their organization—that’s who I want to go to.”

Photos: Dicks Sporting Goods

athlete.bio: A fierce competitor with a relentless spirit, this LSU standout blends agility and precision on the field. Known for her strategic mindset and infectious enthusiasm, she inspires teammates and fans alike.

caption:
My nana passed last Wednesday and I don’t even really know what to say. You don’t ever prepare to lose someone, but man this has hit me harder than I thought possible. 

Nana was the most generous, kind, loving, silly, lovable human. I’ve never met someone with so much genuine joy. You couldn’t help but smile when you were around her. Joy just radiated off of her. She loved like Jesus loves — unconditionally and abundantly. 

She wasn’t a normal nana — she loved super heros and horses and the moon and read a novel a day (I swear). She listened to my music and read every draft of every script and book I’ve ever written. She loved watching me play and was one of my biggest fans and supporters. 
Family was her world. She is so loved and adored by my family. I would do anything to squeeze her one more time. 

I know I’ll get to see her again and that she’s up in heaven dancing with Jesus now but I selfishly just want to talk to her. 
She was ALWAYS there for me. I knew I had her in my corner no matter what and that I always had someone to talk to. 
Hug your people. Time is gift and it’s not promised. 
I find peace in knowing she’s in the arms of her Creator and the fact I’ll get to see her again. But until then I’ll live with all the memories I did get, tucked tight in my heart. 

I’m gonna miss her laugh, her silly jokes, our couch naps, her big beautiful smile, her back scratches, her good morning texts, her opinion and wisdom, cooking with her in the kitchen and holding her hand in the car, and her presence in my life. 

I am broken. I won’t ever be the same. 
Nana — not just a grandparent but my second mom and best friend.
I love you forever and ever. 
❤️ - your #1 Dollbaby

Everything truly does happen for a reason and I now realize that every bit of what I have experienced as a collegiate student athlete has been shaping me for this team, this moment and the future with Great Britain softball. 

This past week was my debut with the team and the wait was 100% worth every second. I found a different type of family within this team, which I will never take for granted.

caption:
Después de ocho años, ha llegado el momento de cerrar una etapa maravillosa en el fcbarcelona. No es fácil despedirse de un lugar que ha sido mucho más que un club: ha sido mi casa, mi escuela y mi familia.

Durante estos años viví momentos que me marcaron para siempre. Tuve el privilegio de vestir esta camiseta, de compartir el vestuario con personas increíbles y de crecer tanto en lo personal como en lo profesional. Me llevo amistades para toda la vida, experiencias únicas y un profundo orgullo por haber formado parte de este club.

Quiero agradecer de corazón a cada persona que ha estado a mi lado en este camino. A mis compañeras, por las risas y el apoyo constante. Al cuerpo técnico y al staff, por creer en mí, por exigirme siempre lo mejor y por acompañarme en cada paso. A los trabajadores del club, desde los que están en el día a día en la ciudad deportiva hasta los que, desde otras áreas, hacen que todo funcione con amor y dedicación.

Y, por supuesto, a los padres y madres por dedicar la mayoría de su tiempo en nosotras. Viajes arriba viajes abajo.

Me voy con el corazón lleno de gratitud y orgullo. Llevaré siempre al Barça en mi alma, porque este club no es solo una camiseta o un escudo, es una forma de entender la vida, de luchar, de nunca rendirse.

Gracias por tanto. Nos volveremos a encontrar.
Visca el Barça, sempre!💙❤️💙❤️💙❤️💙❤️💙

caption:
Nunca pensé que llegaría este momento, pero después de tantos años en el club de mi vida, ha llegado el día en que nuestros caminos se separan. Me siento profundamente agradecida por haber podido crecer, aprender y soñar dentro del Valencia CF, el club donde he vivido algunos de los momentos más especiales de mi vida.

Han sido muchas las vivencias que guardo con cariño, pero lo más valioso que me llevo es a las personas que me han acompañado durante esta etapa. Compañeras, técnicos, trabajadores del club… todos han formado parte de mi camino y a todos les estaré siempre agradecida.

Gracias al cuerpo técnico, fisios, médicos, utilleros, nutricionistas, psicólogos y a todo el staff que, con trabajo y dedicación, hacen posible el día a día. Gracias por creer, por cuidar y por acompañar.

Y gracias, sobre todo, a mi familia, por estar siempre ahí, en cada paso, en cada decisión. Sin vosotros, nada de esto tendría sentido.

No ha sido fácil tomar esta decisión. Dejo una parte muy importante de mí en este escudo. Pero siento que es el momento de seguir creciendo, de abrir nuevas puertas y enfrentar nuevos desafíos personales y futbolísticos.

Gracias por haber hecho de este sueño algo real. Defender esta camiseta ha sido un orgullo que llevaré siempre conmigo.

Amunt Valencia. Gracias por tanto. 🧡🦇

Shoutout to Vitality Labs for welcoming me with open arms into your state of the art recovery facility! With there help I’ve been able to take a massive leap and go harder in my training. #1 priority is taking care of your body. Benefits below ⬇️ 

1. Light Beds (Red Light Therapy Beds):
Light beds use red and near-infrared light to promote cellular repair, improve skin health, reduce inflammation, and support muscle recovery. They are often used by athletes and individuals looking to boost energy, circulation, and collagen production.

2. Salt Light Saunas (Himalayan Salt + Infrared Sauna):
These saunas combine the benefits of infrared heat with Himalayan salt therapy. The infrared heat helps detoxify the body, ease joint and muscle pain, and improve circulation, while the salt air may improve respiratory health and reduce inflammation.

3. Cryotherapy:
Whole-body cryotherapy involves short bursts of exposure to extremely cold temperatures, which can reduce inflammation, speed up muscle recovery, improve mood, boost metabolism, and potentially support better sleep.

4. Zero Gravity Massage Chairs:
These chairs recline the body to a neutral, weightless position that reduces spinal pressure. Combined with full-body massage features, they can relieve muscle tension, enhance circulation, reduce stress, and promote deep relaxation.

athlete.name: Marcos Paz
athlete.bio: Armed with a fierce fastball and sharp curve, this right-handed pitcher combines precision with grit. A fierce competitor, he thrives under pressure, embodying resilience and passion for the game.

caption:
3 1/2 months in to his return to throw program and @marcos_paz06 continues to make great progress hitting his first 90 off the mound this past weekend 🤯

We’ve continued to monitor throw count, velocity, ArmCare numbers, and more on a daily basis as both throwing density and intensity has steadily increased 📈

In the weight room we’ve backed off of volume and have opted for 4-5 shorter workouts each week to account for increased workload on the throwing side while still making sure we are keeping buckets filled 🪣

We have slowly added in new/different stimulus in his throwing to add variability, challenge patterns, increase proprioception, and continue to add stress to the elbow.

Some things we’ve added over the past couple of months and why:

🔵 Heavy plyos (7 & 9oz) — stress levels, constraint/patterning

🔵 Throwing outside — added variables of cleats, uneven ground, wind, etc

🔵 Mini mound — bridge the gap between flat ground and mound work

🔵 Offspeed pitches — get a feel for offspeed pitches at lower intensity

🔵 Athletic / Infield Throws — varying arm slots and distance, off balance, athleticism

🔵 Catch on the mound — bridge between catch and bullpens

🔵 Mound Throws — to a catcher / target with radar feedback

That may seem like a lot but everything is purposeful and progressed with 1 variable being introduced at a time. Progress has been amazing and full bullpens are right around the corner 🗓️

Keep an eye out for more frequent updates over these next few weeks! 

—

1057. 4. 2 & 2. 1. 

1057 days between appearances. 
4 anchors in my pitching shoulder. 
2 surgeries & 2 redshirt years.
1 piece of metal. 

This is my story. This is my testimony. 

Getting to be in the circle again this past month has been surreal, and getting to feel all the love and support from my past and present community made it even more special. To finally make it to the light at the end of the tunnel that I’ve spent over two years chasing feels like finally getting a breath of fresh air. Getting to share that joy and love that comes only from my Lord and Savior in that moment made every step of the journey worthwhile. My story is not over yet and to just say that I am overwhelmed with emotion. My story is written, but I am thankful to be here telling it in the present. 

Full story in the comment section :)

caption:
This past Thursday, I had the incredible honor of serving as a trophy presenter at the NFL Honors Awards—a night dedicated to celebrating the most elite players and coaches in the game. This event was nothing short of spectacular, and I am beyond grateful to have been a part of such a prestigious evening, proudly representing one of the greatest universities in the nation—LSU.💜💛

Throughout the night, I had the privilege of connecting with some of the most accomplished, inspiring, and humble individuals in sports and entertainment.

Coach Prime – Deion Sanders: What an absolute honor to share a conversation with you and witness firsthand the greatness that has defined your legendary career. As one of the most iconic players and coaches to ever grace the game, your wisdom and presence are truly unmatched. Thank you for your time and for setting the standard of excellence. @deionsanders

NFL Hall of Famers – Ray Lewis & Legends: You all were not only larger than life but also incredibly humble, hilarious, and down-to-earth. Your dedication, perseverance, and unmatched skill have set the bar for generations of athletes. It was an honor to be in your presence and to celebrate your legacies. Thank you for everything you’ve given to the game! 🐐 @raylewis 

Nikki Glaser: Your energy is electric! You exude confidence, kindness, and authenticity, making you such an inspiring role model for young women everywhere. You were so easy to talk to, and I admire how you’ve paved your own path in the entertainment industry with grace and resilience. Keep shining! 🤍 @nikkiglaser 

Above all, I’m deeply grateful—for the opportunity, the experience, and the incredible people I met. Representing LSU on such a grand stage and celebrating football’s finest was an unforgettable honor.

caption:
Let’s talk about it!

Getting back to your sport after an off-season is so hard—especially when it comes to not critically critiquing yourself. It’s a mental battle of comparing who you were before the break to how you look and feel now.

Giving yourself grace and having patience when coming back as an elite athlete is HARD. But let’s be real: if you haven’t been getting these reps for over a month, how can you expect to still be as good as you were when you left? That’s not fair to YOU.

It’s important to see and feel these things to jumpstart some motivation heading into the spring season, but is your self-talk and comparison healthy? I converted that attention into intention. I reflected on what I had learned and what I know to be true about the process of doing each drill. I turned it into a competition with myself—seeing how consistent I could be in the process—and with that, I saw success.

So, how are you being patient with yourself and giving yourself grace?
How are you attacking reps with intention?

These principles apply to all areas of life!

#expectationvsreality #d1 #volleyball

You’re racing with a Lamborghini, but you show up late to the race and lose to other cars that shouldn’t even compare. (A Ford Fusion 🤣)

You can train your swing to get off the starting line and beat the other cars. Quickness, readiness and body control

You may need to get extreme a little (like this 20ft away machine drill)

People may look at you weird in the facility / cage
